title: A Low-Power, Low-Noise, High-Performance Re-Convergent Clock Mesh Design for Large AI Compute Clusters
problem: Large AI compute clusters require globally synchronous single-clock-domain design for high performance, but traditional clock networks (flex-H tree, forwarded spine) cannot meet the low-power, low-noise requirements for complex AI processors.
motivation: Modern AI ICs with large compute clusters need high-performance global clock distribution at low power consumption with minimal noise. Single clock domain requires robust mesh topology suitable for high-frequency operation.
method: A re-convergent clock mesh distributes the timing signal throughout a large AI processor through paths that branch out and then reconverge (rejoin), reducing power consumption and electrical noise compared to traditional designs like flex-H trees and forwarded spines. This was verified using HSPICE electrical simulation and PrimeTime timing analysis.
key_novelty: A re-convergent clock mesh (where timing-signal paths branch out and then rejoin) achieves 20% lower power consumption at a given clock speed, or runs 20% faster at the same power level.
contributions: Novel re-convergent clock mesh topology for AI compute clusters
20% power reduction at target operating frequency
Comparison with traditional clock network architectures
limitations: Silicon results mention QoR improvements but lack detailed power, frequency, and area metrics. Limited scope to clock distribution only.
primary_theme: Clock network design for AI accelerators
